Critiques of Modernization Theory

Ideological critique

Forgotten the colonial history

Today’s developing/underdeveloped countries are facing a DIFFERENT WORLD than the pre-industrial Western countries when they started their “take-offs”.

The so-called “modernization” is a justification for interfering in poor countries’ internal affairs.

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology12 / 38
The Dependency Theory: The Exploitive World System

An integration of several different theories (neocolonialism, world system theory, Neo-Marxism theory);

Major propositions:

Globalization: today’s countries are increasingly interdependent;

Unequal economic interdependency and exploitive world system: Wealthy (core) countries take advantage of the cheap labor and raw materials in the less powerful (periphery) countries, and sell their high profit product back to those countries.

Class distinction: Power Elites of both wealthy and poor countries coalesce to maintain the exploitive world system;

Ideological justification: This system is justified by the Ideology of Capitalism (“free market values”, “efficiency”, “trickle-down effect”, “deregulation”, “privatization”, etc.)

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology13 / 38
Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry, Co., Ltd.): the world’s largest contract electronics manufacturer. It manufactures computers, consumer electronics, communications, and other products, including connectors, cable assemblies, enclosures, flat-panel displays, game consoles, motherboards, servers, and televisions. Foxconn suicide spate: Jan.-Nov./2010, 18 Foxconn employees attempted suicide with 14 deaths. The long-covered workplace perils began to be bombarded by the media. In response to the media coverage, Foxconn substantially increased wages for its Shenzhen factory workforce, installed suicide-prevention netting, and asked employees to sign no-suicide pledges. Workers were also forced to sign a legally binding document guaranteeing that they and their descendants would not sue the company as a result of unexpected death, self-injury, or suicide.

Case Study:

Foxconn

The company also contracts with 329 apparel manufacturers operating in 38 countries. China is its largest source of apparel at 28%, followed by Vietnam with 23% and Thailand at 12%

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology29 / 38
Pou Chen Corporation

Pou Chen Corporation is the largest manufacturer of branded athletic and casual footwear in the world. Its customers include Nike, Adidas, Asics, New Balance, and Timberland. It makes more than 300 million pairs of shoes annually and accounts for roughly 20% of the global wholesale value of branded athletic and casual footwear.

Pou Chen was founded in Taiwan. It has factories in China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, and Myanmar.

In addition to producing footwear, the company sells sportswear under its own YYSports brand in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.

Is the international outsourcing a form of economic assistance, or exploitation?

Class Discussion:

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology33 / 38
Slide 33

The Question: Are the following things helping the poor countries?

International Outsourcing: the contracting out of a business process to a third-party in another country, usually a developing country due to its cheap labors.

Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): an enterprise has set up long-term relations with foreign company, provides it with technical assistance and financing, and most importantly, possesses ownership and interests.

[an investment made by a firm or individual in one country into business interests located in another country]
